description: Stock nginx 1.30.6 default merge_slashes routing between global and individual task histories, with original and normalized URI diagnostics.

configuration: # Leave merge_slashes unset: this recording exercises nginx's default, on.
nginx: the configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf syntax is ok
nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf test is successful

substitutions: Current nginx 1.30.6 stands in for the service's 2016 gateway. merge_slashes is deliberately unset to test its default-on behavior; this is not a recording of that historical deployment.

Two exact-match locations return synthetic service-shaped JSON histories. nginx itself normalizes the URI and selects the location; no application code merges slashes. Authentication and the full business application are outside this probe.

X-Request-Uri, X-Normalized-Uri and X-Query-String are diagnostic response headers added only for this recording. They expose nginx variables; the imitating service does not promise them. Empty query strings omit X-Query-String.
The scope is adjacent-slash routing and preservation of slashes in query data. Percent decoding, dot segments, trailing-slash redirects and other nginx normalization rules are not covered.
client: scripts/record.mjs: raw HTTP/1.1 requests over a TCP socket to the container's ephemeral loopback port.

exchanges.name: global-control
exchanges.description: The ordinary global-history path selects both tasks.

exchanges.name: empty-id
exchanges.description: An empty task id leaves two slashes and selects global history after nginx normalization.

exchanges.name: many-slashes
exchanges.description: Several adjacent runs compress before exact location selection.

exchanges.name: query-slashes
exchanges.description: Path slashes merge while slash runs in the raw query stay intact.

exchanges.name: task-control
exchanges.description: A valid task id selects only its individual history.

exchanges.name: task-slashes
exchanges.description: Repeated slashes around a valid task id still select that individual history.
